_comment: Settings for the documentation site that cannot be derived from what is
published.
COMPONENTS. The C++ libraries and the Python libraries ship on independent
release lines -- CCCL is on 3.x while cuda-cccl is on its own line -- so
each gets its own subtree and its own version switcher. A reader picks one
from the landing page at the site root.
'path' is the directory the component lives under, relative to the site
root. C++ deliberately sits at the root with an empty path: it has been
published there since before this scheme existed, and moving it would break
every documentation URL that currently works. Python is new to versioning,
so it starts nested.
VERSIONS ARE NOT LISTED HERE. Within each component they are discovered from
the directories that exist on the published site, so publishing a version is
all it takes for it to appear in that component's switcher. A directory
counts only once it contains an index.html, so a failed or partial upload is
not advertised. To retire a version, delete its directory from gh-pages.
'latest_stable' is the one thing that stays a human decision, per component.
Publishing a release is not the same as declaring it the version readers
land on by default: during a release candidate period, or when a build turns
out to be wrong, you want the former without the latter. It is the target
for that component's landing redirect, for its /latest/ alias, and for
legacy unversioned URLs beneath it. Keep it null until a stable version has
actually been published. If it names a version that is not published it is
ignored with a warning, rather than redirecting readers to a 404.
RETENTION: GitHub Pages refuses to publish a site larger than 1 GB. A built
C++ version measures 110-290 MB -- older releases are the expensive ones,
because they rebuild against current Sphinx. The Python docs are around
1.5 MB, so they are effectively free and the budget is really about C++.
'size_budget_versions' is a rough guard on the number of directories across
all components; exceeding it warns rather than fails, because the remedy is
a decision about which release to drop.
